To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the monomeric, compactly folded DHQ synthase from Aspergillus is a highly efficient monofunctional enzyme, which can be used as a model to investigate the catalytic mechanism of the penta-functional enzyme.
a monomeric and monofunctional form of DHQ synthase can be produced by truncating the N-termini of the AROM proteins from A. nidulans or N. crassa.
the N-terminally truncated, monofunctionally active AROM protein of A. nidulans retains the properties of the intact enzyme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the structure and function of the AROM protein, which catalyses the first four steps of the shikimate pathway, and is a key regulatory protein in aromatic amino acid biosynthesis.
the characterization of the monofunctionally active dehydroquinate (DHQ) synthase domain of the A. nidulans AROM protein.

the elucidation of the structural and functional relationships of the individual domains within the pentafunctional protein, and the monomeric domain reported here has the potential to serve as a model system in this investigation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the monofunctionnal domain of the Aspergillus AROM protein is monomeric in solution, and has a native-like conformation, and retains the same catalytic properties as the intact penta-functional AROM protein of N. crassa.
the monofunctionnal DHQ synthase derived from A. nidulans is a stable, monomeric, compact, globular, active, monofunctionnal enzyme.
the monofunctionals AROM protein of A. nidulans is monomeric, has a compact globule conformation, and is catalytically active.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N-terminal domain of the penta-functional AROM protein of A. nidulans is monofunctional and monomeric, but is a compactly folded protein that retains full catalytic activity.
the DHQ synthase functional domain from the AROM protein of A. nidulans is a monomeric enzyme with an active site that is structurally similar to that of the intact penta-functional enzyme.
the DHQ synthase activity of the A. nidulans pentafunctional ARO protein is a compact, monomeric protein that is efficiently active as an independent domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, despite its small size and the absence of the other four functional domains of the penta-functional AROM protein, the monofunctionally active DHQ synthase retains its compact structure and catalytic activity.
the monofunctionals are active and compact, but the intact pentafunctionals are much more efficient, presumably due to allosteric regulation.
the monofunctionnal DHQ synthase derived from A. nidulans is active and compactly folded in the absence of the rest of the AROM protein.
